name: adopt
context_rationale: The skill asks the user questions one at a time, waits for answers, and co-derives the vault contents from live conversation — it cannot complete its brownfield interview or mode selection without back-and-forth in the main thread.
summary: Onboards the AI SDLC pipeline into an existing codebase by scanning it with code-review-graph, optionally running /diagnose, conducting a structured brownfield interview, and producing an initial vault (concept.json, risk-register.json, CLAUDE.md, optional backlog.md and ADRs) that reflects code reality rather than doc claims. It can also invoke /slice-candidates to build a backlog from confirmed /diagnose findings. The skill replaces /triage for brownfield projects and sets up the vault for the normal /slice loop.

name: slice-candidates
context_rationale: The default path is a mechanical pass — run build_backlog.py against diagnose-out/ inputs and emit backlog.md — with no dependency on conversation history; the --obo mode is interactive but bounded to structured AskUserQuestion calls that do not need accumulated thread context.
summary: Reads an annotated diagnosis.html (produced by /diagnose and round-tripped through the repo owner), extracts confirmed findings, and uses build_backlog.py to produce a DAG-ordered backlog.md of slice candidates. It uses code-review-graph blast-radius queries to detect file-overlap coupling between candidates, topo-sorts them by dependency plus a severity/blast/effort priority score, and detects must-do-together cycles. An optional --obo mode walks the owner through findings one at a time via structured prompts and writes a diagnosis.annotated.html before building the backlog.

methodology_tools.name: scripts.lib.product_scope

name: query-design
context_rationale: The skill is an interactive, back-and-forth Q&A conversation that follows up on user questions, drills down iteratively, and optionally offers a handoff to /slice based on what emerged in the session — it fundamentally depends on the accumulated conversation context.
summary: Holds a read-only, grounded Q&A conversation about an existing codebase, answering questions by reading actual code via Grep, Read, and code-review-graph queries rather than recall. Every answer cites specific file/line/symbol evidence. It changes nothing — no writes, no file creation, no vault mutations. If the conversation surfaces a concrete actionable finding, it offers (but never forces) a single delegated handoff to /slice.
